recipe.notes:
Pointwise cross-encoder scored at the last position: served score = sigmoid((W_yes - W_no)
. h_last) with an fp32 head; yes=9693, no=2152 (the snapshot vocab, equal to the repo's
1_LogitScore/config.json; matches classifier_from_token ["no", "yes"] order). The recipe
targets the card's transformers-script referent (sigmoid, default instruction "Given a search
query, retrieve relevant candidates that answer the query."), not the sentence-transformers
referent (config_sentence_transformers.json declares Identity activation = raw logits and a
different default prompt).

Instruction policy (declared): the client never sends the /rerank instruction field
(instruction: none) and the engine's template default -- the card's default instruction --
is pinned as fixed frame text in the template. The declared render therefore matches the
engine for every request the client sends. A run that needs a different instruction must ship
a new template file and a new recipe (a changed frame is a new judgement family and never
pools with this one).

Served template (template.jinja): vLLM v0.31.0's qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja with its two
expression blocks rewritten to the recipe variable convention (query, document, instruction)
and a messages fallback, so the file renders byte-identically both the way the harness's
stage-1 template check calls it and the way the engine calls it (messages + the instruction
chat-template kwarg; verified equal against the untouched upstream file). The file must
ship with the recipe -- without --chat-template the engine logs a startup warning
(is_original_qwen3_reranker is set) and falls back to un-templated pair encoding; the
per-request ChatTemplateResolutionError path degrades scores silently.

Media policy (the pixel pin, both halves). Serve: serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins min_pixels 4096 /
max_pixels 1310720 under the nested images_kwargs scope -- ONE shape across the media
recipes, decided from the v0.31.0 tag source (the nested dict reaches the HF processor's
images_kwargs and the vLLM-side image token budget; the flat form also re-sizes every video
clip): the reference script's own numbers, so the engine and the reference resize identically
by construction (the repo's preprocessor default min_pixels 4095 can tip one image token for
thin strips). Image-token budget: 1280 tokens/image at max_pixels (px/1024 after the 2x2
merge). Capacity: one media item per request (serve.limit_mm_per_prompt image=1;
client.max_images 1 carries the same number) -- an image on the query side or on one
document side, never two in one request, so the engine's multi-item guard is never crossed
(a side carrying text plus >= 2 images bypasses it: the engine hoists placeholders to the
front of the side and joins the texts with a newline, which the reference cannot express;
declared, unmeasured). Client half: image_processor qwen3_vl and client.image_policy with the
same pixel numbers and engine_pixel_pinning true -- the declaration that admits the card's
4096 px floor below the family's stock 65536 px -- so the client resizes every image as the
card's process_vision_info does (qwen-vl-utils smart_resize, factor 32) and counts it as the
engine does; an image rides its side as {"content": [image, text]}, one pair per request. The
harness's media stage holds the client's sent images (count, placement, prepared geometry,
tokens) to reference.py --mode media and, against the engine, the engine's media count to the
client's. The pin restates the checkpoint's own budget (preprocessor_config.json min_pixels 4095 /
max_pixels 1310720): an unpinned engine keeps every image the client prepares under 4096..1310720,
so the negative control that unpins it changes nothing and does not apply (said so in the wave's
control report); an engine pinned to other numbers fails the media stage's engine count.

Video: out of scope (input: [text, image]). A sibling recipe declaring video follows the one
video-policy decision (qwen3-vl-embedding-2b: 64 uniformly spaced frames per clip, the
container sent as video_url with the engine pinned via --media-io-kwargs); this reference
refuses video-bearing rows loudly rather than sampling them at any default.

Empty sides: the recipe pins empty_doc send_text with the card's own "NULL" placeholder
(empty_doc_text "NULL") as the declared policy; the wired rerank client applies
empty_doc/empty_doc_text before shipping, so the served render of an empty side is the card's
"NULL" like the reference's (a bare '<Document>:' side was measured to diverge).
An empty QUERY is refused by the product's empty_query: refuse default (the typed DataError
names the query id); this recipe keeps that default -- an empty query is a data error
upstream, never a silent default. A whitespace-only query is not empty, to the card as to the
client: the card's format_mm_content keeps any non-empty text verbatim, the client sends it,
and reference.py renders it as the card does.

Budgets: the pair fit binds on overflow and the rerank client settles the query at
query_max_tokens (4096) whenever the query exceeds its share, even when the pair fits. The
card cuts its own way: it keeps every special token and the first 8192 - specials non-special
tokens of all but the last 5 ids, then re-appends those 5 (the assistant tail) -- so it keeps
the anchor, keeps an over-share query whole, and admits up to 8197 tokens; reference.py
renders that cut and never the client's. Hence over_cap_cut_differs: the anchor kept, the
content cut differently. The exception, precisely: when the query alone fills the card's body
(about 8100 query tokens or more), the card's cut lands inside the query, and the non-special
fixed text after it -- "\n<Document>:" -- is dropped together with the whole document, while
every special token and the assistant tail stay. No anchor is lost (the frame text is not the
model's read-out position), so the label stays, with this exception declared here; the client
never ships such a pair (its query settles at 4096).

What the harness does: every pair the client changed (its processing record: the query
settled at its 4096-token share, which changes every pair of the row, or a budget cut counted
with the 66-token frame) is reported in the non-gating table under the declared deviation;
every other pair gates exactly.

Stage 1 on CPU proves: the declared pair shape renders byte-identically to the served
template file (and hence to the card's reference prompt), the anchors survive every
over-length cut, and on the pairs rows the client's spans equal the card's (the reference
subprocess's render, the card's own cut). The GPU wave
(stages 2-3) must still check: score-level equivalence against the ~4.0 GB weights, the
engine's /tokenize agreement, the template mount (T0), and image-expansion token counts.

Per-size facts, read at the pinned revision. Architecture: Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration (config.json:architectures); text_config.hidden_size 4096, 36 layers, 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, intermediate_size 12288, max_position_embeddings 262144, tie_word_embeddings false (config.json:tie_word_embeddings); vision_config.depth 27, hidden_size 1152, deepstack_visual_indexes [8, 16, 24] (config.json:vision_config). Context: the card's Model Overview table says 32K and the family's serve.max_model_len 32768 is that number (the checkpoint's config allows 262144); no served request reaches the cap (client.max_tokens 8192). Weights: bfloat16 at the top level (config.json:dtype; text_config and vision_config declare float32, exactly as the 2b row's do -- the card script's from_pretrained resolves the top-level dtype), 17,534,247,392 B = 16.33 GiB in 4 shards (model.safetensors.index.json:metadata.total_size); embeddings untied (config.json:tie_word_embeddings false), so the score head is built from lm_head's own yes/no rows; KV at 32768 tokens is 2 x 36 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B/token x 32768 = 4.83 GB = 4.5 GiB, so bf16 weights + KV fit one 80 GB-class GPU (resources.gpus 1, the family's). One forward of 32768 tokens stays inside the 32-bit envelope: attention q 32 x 128 x 32768 x 2 B = 2.7e8 B, MLP activations 12288 x 32768 = 4.0e8 elements; the served budget (8192) is below max_model_len, so a full-budget request is not the chunked full-context case. Score head: the same yes/no construction as the 2b row (1_LogitScore/config.json:true_token_id 9693, :false_token_id 2152, JSON-equal); modules.json names its module directory 1_CausalScoreHead where the 2b names 1_LogitScore -- both entries declare the same sentence_transformers.cross_encoder.modules.logit_score.LogitScore class, and the file the reference cross-checks (1_LogitScore/config.json) is present with the same ids, so the served score is sigmoid((W_yes - W_no) . h_last) as the family declares. Family membership, every file byte- or JSON-identical to the 2b row at its own pinned revision: tokenizer.json (sha256 aeb13307...), chat_template.jinja (sha256 3636d0f0...), additional_chat_templates/reranker.jinja (sha256 47c758cb...), config_sentence_transformers.json, sentence_bert_config.json, preprocessor_config.json (4095..1310720 px; the recipe's pin raises the floor to 4096), video_preprocessor_config.json (video is out of scope: input [text, image]), and the card script scripts/qwen3_vl_reranker.py (byte-identical at every variant's pinned revision; reference.py re-implements it; sha256 bd5d2f5d...: MAX_LENGTH 8192, the same truncation and the same default instruction). The family's ONE reference loads this row's checkpoint from the harness's --tokenizer spec (the variant's model@revision) and its tokenizer's own 1_LogitScore/config.json.
